# Build contract: chapters 3 and 4

Owner: creative-director. The shared plan for building chapter 3 (Regional Office) and chapter 4 (Southie) at the same time. Read this file, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md and your chapter spec. Delete this file after the integration branch merges to `main`.

## Branches

- Integration branch: `agent/creative-director/c3c4`, cut from `main` at `de70d3b`. It holds this file and the stubbed props.
- Each agent works in its own worktree, on its own branch cut from the integration branch:

| Agent | Model | Branch | Owns in this build |
|---|---|---|---|
| systems-dev | sonnet | `agent/systems-dev/c3c4` | `src/core/`, `src/systems/` (the "Systems" list below) |
| creative-director | fable | `agent/creative-director/c3c4-art` | `src/art/` (every STUB in `src/art/propsC34.ts`, and any new NPC looks), missing dialogue |
| level-builder (chapter 3) | sonnet | `agent/level-builder/c3` | `src/chapters/03/`, chapter 3 lines in `src/ui/` and `src/audio/` if any |
| level-builder (chapter 4) | sonnet | `agent/level-builder/c4` | `src/chapters/04/`, chapter 4 lines in `src/ui/` and `src/audio/` if any |

- Commit to your own branch only. Never commit to `main` or to the integration branch, and never push. The main session merges finished branches into the integration branch.
- To pick up work that has landed on the integration branch (for example, systems), merge `agent/creative-director/c3c4` into your branch.
- Before you report done: `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build` pass on your branch.
- `src/chapters/index.ts` registers chapters. Each level-builder adds only its own `registerChapter` line. The main session resolves the one-line conflict.

## Props (creative-director draws, level-builders place)

The keys, sizes and meanings are in `src/art/propsC34.ts`, spread into `PROP`, so `PROP.portacabin`, `PROP.filingCabinet.shut`, `PROP.container.mas4471` and the rest already compile. Each is a plain outlined block marked `// STUB` until the creative director draws it.

- Level-builders: place these names now. Do not add keys. If you need a prop that is not in the list, use the nearest existing `PROP` and list what you needed in your report.
- Creative-director: replace every STUB at the size given. A size changes only by editing this file and telling the main session.
- Props that already exist and fit: `PROP.skip`, `PROP.van`, `PROP.dartboard`, `PROP.noticeboard`, `PROP.kettle`, `PROP.bins`, `PROP.crate`, `PROP.bottleCrate`, `PROP.barrel`, `PROP.cardboardBox`, `PROP.weapon.clipboard`, `PROP.weapon.shillelagh`, `PROP.steam`. The forklift is the boss sprite `boss.c3.boss.halloran` (`src/art/machines.ts`); the foreman is `boss.c4.boss.foreman` (`src/art/cast.ts`).
- Tiles: chapter 3 is region `kilnamoe` (`yardConcrete`, `floor`, `fence`, `cover`, `counter`, walls). Chapter 4 is region `cities` (`barWood`, `greenWall`, `containerRed`, `containerBlue`, `rail`, `floodlit`, `dockEdge`, `water`, and the rest in `src/art/tiles.ts`). If a screen needs a tile the region lacks, ask the creative director through your report.

## Systems (systems-dev builds; level-builders use them once merged)

The names and shapes below are fixed so level-builders can write against them. systems-dev may add fields but not rename. Each needs unit tests.

1. **Slide puzzle** (`PuzzleKind` `containers`, chapter 4). In `src/core/chapter.ts`:

   ```ts
   export interface SlideRail {
     readonly id: string;
     /** Top-left tile of slot 0. */
     readonly origin: TileCoord;
     /** Which way the slots run: 'across' steps right a piece-length per slot, 'along' steps down. */
     readonly axis: 'across' | 'along';
     readonly slots: number;
     /** The piece's size in tiles: `length` along the axis, `breadth` across it. */
     readonly length: number;
     readonly breadth: number;
     /** The slot the piece starts in. */
     readonly start: number;
     /** PROP frame for the piece. */
     readonly frame: string;
   }
   export interface SlidePuzzlePlacement {
     readonly sectionId: PuzzleSectionId;
     readonly screenId: ScreenId;
     readonly rails: readonly SlideRail[];
     /** E on the examinable pulls the lever: its rail's piece moves one slot on, wrapping from the last slot to 0. */
     readonly levers: readonly { readonly examinableId: string; readonly railId: string; readonly propId?: string }[];
     /** The slot each rail's piece must be in. Met, the section completes. completeNow() moves them there. */
     readonly goal: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;
   }
   // ChapterModule gains: readonly slidePuzzles?: readonly SlidePuzzlePlacement[];
   ```

   Pieces are solid to Andrew and slide over `TUNING.world.pushSlideMs`. A lever's `propId` flips between `PROP.lever.up` and `.down` on each pull. A half-finished puzzle resets on a load, as the push puzzles do. Emits a pull event the audio layer can use.

2. **Boss controls** on `BossRunner` (`src/systems/boss.ts`):
   - `guard(tag: string, side: 'front' | null): void`. While `front`, a player hit from within 90° either side of the body's facing does no damage and emits `boss:guarded` `{ bossId, tag }`. Halloran's pallet shield.
   - `pin(tag: string, at: Vec2 | null): void`. A pinned body stays at `at`, faces Andrew, and neither moves nor attacks; it can still be hit. `null` releases it. The foreman in his control box.
   - `forcePhase(phaseId: string): void`. Jumps to a phase now (fires `onPhaseChanged`). Knocking the foreman off the box.
   - `daze(tag, ms)` already exists: use it for the forks sticking in a crate stack.

3. **Sweep hazard** on `ChapterContext`:

   ```ts
   sweepHazard(opts: {
     readonly from: Vec2;
     readonly to: Vec2;
     /** Width of the swept band, px. */
     readonly width: number;
     /** The shadow shows along the whole path this long before anything moves, ms. */
     readonly telegraphMs: number;
     /** Time to travel from `from` to `to`, ms. */
     readonly travelMs: number;
     /** The meter hit on contact: a weight from `TUNING.overhaul.hitWeights`. */
     readonly weight: 'ordinary' | 'heavy' | 'worst';
     readonly knockback: number;
     /** What is drawn moving and its shadow. */
     readonly frame: string;
     readonly shadowFrame: string;
   }): Promise<void>; // resolves when the pass ends; a bar return or dispose cancels it
   ```

   Hits Andrew at most once per pass. The crane's container in chapter 4. Enemies are not hurt by it.

4. **Leashed enemies** in fights. `FightPlacement` gains `readonly zones?: readonly { readonly enemyId: EnemyId; readonly area: AreaRect }[]`. Enemies of that id spawn inside their zone and never leave it, so they fight at range from there. Chapter 3's box-throwing `worker`s on the gantry.

5. **Line of sight for scripts.** `ChapterContext.lineClear(from: Vec2, to: Vec2, width: number): boolean`: true when a band `width` wide from `from` to `to` touches no blocked tile, solid prop, puzzle piece or NPC. Then replace the hand-made dog check in chapter 2's `maybeStumbleLesson` (`src/chapters/02/script.ts`) with it. That one function is yours for this.

6. **Check, and fix if needed:** the deduction board can link a clue found in an earlier chapter (chapter 3's board uses `c2.clue.fragment`; chapter 4's uses `c3.clue.manifest`), and evidence carries over between chapters.

## Chapters (level-builders)

- Build your chapter to its spec in `docs/chapters/`, following how `src/chapters/01/` and `src/chapters/02/` are built: maps, index, script, objectives with hints, the bar with its hot-drink dispenser and steam (`urn.steam` pattern; chapter 3 uses `PROP.kettle`, chapter 4 the bar's tea), returns to the bar, Myko calls, and the closing scene.
- All text is already written in `src/content/dialogue/c03.ts` and `c04.ts`. Use those IDs. Do not write or change player-visible text. If a line you need is missing, use the nearest existing one and list the missing ID with what it should say in your report.
- All numbers go in `src/content/tuning.ts`; the bosses and fights for both chapters are already there.
- Breakables: scattered singles, pairs and small heaps, never in rows; never on wall tiles; never in the way of a route. The placement test in `tests/unit/playtest6.test.ts` checks chapters 1 and 2; qa will add yours.
- Until the systems branch lands, build everything that does not need items 1 to 5 above. Then merge the integration branch and wire them in.
- Leave `tests/` to qa, except where an existing test breaks because of your chapter.

## After the four branches land

The main session merges systems, art, chapter 3 and chapter 4 into the integration branch, then qa (sonnet) writes the chapter 3 and 4 tests and a scripted playthrough of each. Then the owner plays it and decides on the merge to `main`.
